clue.text: Such folk wisdom's views lead lots astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these three words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Folk wisdom is criticised for its views leading many people into error.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'wisdom' stands for 'is', a link between definition and wordplay; the definition is singular in form but describes the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional sayings and superstitions passed down orally are folk wisdom by nature.

clue.text: Concerning British, a weapon put in to destabilise

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in an argument over money
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: A British weapon was brought in to unsettle the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something lose its balance and tip over is to destabilise it.

clue.text: One certainly can't have it? Don't be so sure!

definitions.meaning: uncertainty, which a person who is certain cannot have
an imperative telling someone to question something

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves is told not to be so confident.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt is the lack of certainty, and to doubt is to be unsure.

clue.text: Rile badly about basic change, being easily upset

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled rile wraps round the other anagram
badly signals the word rile is put together wrongly
change signals the letters of basic are rearranged

explanation.surface: Upsetting someone over a fundamental change makes them touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work at once: 'badly' on the outer word, 'change' on the inner; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irascible is quick-tempered, quickly angered or put out.

clue.text: Beg for attenuated course, having a limited time

indicators.note: attenuated means thinned or shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
T is the abbreviation for time, and limited suggests abbreviated

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a short course of study in limited time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attenuated' cuts ENTREE to ENTRE; 'for' and 'having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or ask earnestly, so to beg.

clue.text: Rainbow, say, seen in West End, north of Waterloo

indicators.note: north of means above, so in this down clue that letter sits on top
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a Waterloo is a crushing defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: A rainbow is spotted over central London, north of Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like the London district, but it means the last letter of 'West'; 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow is a species of this freshwater fish, so it is an example.

clue.text: Basis of successful partnership in test? Nothing tops that

indicators.note: tops means sits above, so in this down clue nothing is placed first

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis
a test is a match, as in cricket's Test match

explanation.surface: A test of a partnership, where nothing beats mutual affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'that' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage based on romantic affection is the foundation of a good partnership.

clue.text: Main position taken by Berkeley, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Bishop George Berkeley held a see, a bishop's diocese and position

explanation.surface: The philosopher Berkeley takes a particular position.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkeley was an 18th-century Irish philosopher who was Bishop of Cloyne; a bishop's position is his see.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old poetic word for the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Backed rising, with monarch imprisoned, to form republic

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so the monarch is shut within the other piece
backed means turned back to front, so the word for rising is read backwards

parts.note: rising means going up
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A rebellion, backed by a rising, jails the king and sets up a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like the reversal signal, but it is the fodder (UP); 'Backed' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American country is a republic, a state with an elected head rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Ran out wildly holding eyepiece no longer in style

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the scrambled letters wrap round the other piece
wildly signals the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the uvea is a part, a piece, of the eye

explanation.surface: Someone flees in a hurry clutching an outdated monocle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges RAN OUT into ARTNOU, and 'holding' puts UVEA (a layer of the eye) inside it, before the final U.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative movement of around 1890 to 1910, long since out of fashion, so a style no longer current.

clue.text: Old boy's story gripping many in bar

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil; the possessive gives S

indicators.note: gripping means holding tight, so the story wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many

explanation.surface: A former pupil's anecdote holds the crowd in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the definition (a barrier), not the pub the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar across a path is a barrier, something that blocks the way.

clue.text: Distinctive quality of British in a certain period

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a period

parts.note: a time is a certain period

explanation.surface: Something characteristically British belongs to a particular era.
explanation.definitionFit: The tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another is its characteristic quality.

clue.text: Part of welfare state mentioned in declaration, in other words

indicators.note: part of signals the letters are a portion of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A section of the welfare state is mentioned in a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something again in different wording is exactly a declaration put another way.

clue.text: Pieces of chintz are ordered in this way — for wool it's the opposite

definitions.text: Pieces of chintz are ordered in this way — for wool it's the opposite

parts.words: Pieces of chintz are ordered in this way — for wool it's the opposite
parts.note: the pieces are the letters: C H I N T Z run in dictionary order, while W O O L runs in exactly the reverse order

explanation.surface: Fabric scraps are sorted one way, woollen ones the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sorting fabric; the 'pieces' are in fact the letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters arranged as in the dictionary order A to Z are in that order.

clue.text: Solicitous inquiry involving way in which rugby, initially, is reported

parts.note: how means the way in which

indicators.note: is reported means spoken aloud, giving words that sound like the letters

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a rugby game went.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the letters R U sound like two words of a greeting; 'involving' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous question after someone's health or well-being shows concern for them.

clue.text: A counter I arranged for drink

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a bar counter for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-flavoured French liqueur, so a drink.

clue.text: Launch to ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a standard abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A launch is when a ship goes into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something is to throw it, which is to launch it.

clue.text: Understand refusal to divide a lot of power

indicators.note: dividing splits something, so the refusal goes into the middle of the power unit

parts.note: KW, kilowatt, is a thousand watts, a lot of power
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A rejection splits a powerful bloc, and one must grasp why.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to understand or grasp it.

clue.text: Typical male Times reader who lives in a castle

definitions.text: Typical male Times reader who lives in a castle

parts.words: Typical male Times reader who lives in a castle
parts.note: recalls the saying that a man of this nation's home is his castle, and The Times is a London paper

explanation.surface: A stereotypical newspaper reader lives grandly in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'an Englishman's home is his castle' means a man is master in his own house.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the country where The Times is published, proverbially master in his own home.

clue.text: Information boy provided in relation to class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy supplies information about his class at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole genus or category rather than one member.

clue.text: Lack of resources in planet on edge of destruction

indicators.note: on means following, so the planet comes after the letter
the edge of a word is its opening letter here

parts.note: Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: The world is short of resources and teetering on the brink of ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'on' puts EARTH after D, the first letter of 'destruction'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, a shortage of something needed.

clue.text: Back university of religious type

parts.note: hind means back or rear, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: A religious person supports the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main faith of India is a person of a particular religion.

clue.text: Legal workers of sort Leo is, for example

definitions.meaning: lawyers who witness and certify documents

definitions.text: of sort Leo is, for example
definitions.meaning: Split the answer three and five

explanation.surface: Lawyers of a certain kind, like Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as NOT ARIES: the zodiac sign Leo is an example of a sign other than Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are officials authorised to certify deeds and contracts, so legal workers.

clue.text: Talk at length but inconclusively as legal scholar

indicators.note: inconclusively means without a conclusion, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rabbit, as in rabbit on, is British slang for chatter

explanation.surface: A legal scholar talks endlessly but never reaches a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word; RABBIT loses its last letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish teacher of religious law is a scholar of that law.

clue.text: Producer of fruit eaten by rani, mostly cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and altered, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Fruit from a tree is cooked and eaten by an Indian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RANI to RAN; 'cooked' rearranges EATEN BY RAN. A rani is an Indian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian fig tree bears small figs, so it is a producer of fruit.

clue.text: Something over my head — with no end of puzzlement, finally I get it!

indicators.note: with no end of means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a hat is something worn over one's head

explanation.surface: Something baffling is beyond someone, until at last they grasp it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over my head' suggests not understanding, but it means a hat on top. A HAT loses its last letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation uttered when understanding dawns after being puzzled.

clue.text: Disheartened fighter, once our enemy

indicators.note: disheartened means losing its heart, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter

explanation.surface: A demoralised fighter was once an enemy of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes X, the heart of BOXER. The Boers fought the British in South Africa around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaner farmers who fought the British in the Boer Wars were Britain's foes historically.

clue.text: One doing needlework for therapy?

parts.note: needlework suggests sewing as a calming hobby, but here it is inserting needles into the body to treat ailments

explanation.surface: Someone takes up sewing to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of the Chinese medical practice treats patients by inserting fine needles.
